content.title: Austin Reaves Injury Report: Will He Play In Lakers Vs. Rockets Game 1?
content.text: Daniel AlamedaBased in Cincinnati, Ohio, from Somis, California. Attended Arizona State University. Don't just yell into an abyss, send me an email and let's talk.Austin Reaves Injury Report: Will He Play in Lakers vs. Rockets Game 1? The Los Angeles Lakers tip off their Western Conference first-round series against the Houston Rockets tonight, April 18, 2026, at Crypto.com Arena — and they’ll be doing it severely shorthanded. Austin Reaves has been ruled out for Game 1 with a Grade 2 left oblique strain. The team is targeting early May for his return, which almost certainly means he’ll sit out the entire first-round series. Combined with the confirmed absence of Luka Dončić, sidelined by a Grade 2 left hamstring strain he suffered on April 2, Los Angeles is heading into the playoffs without the two players who led the team in scoring for much of the season. Together, Dončić and Reaves averaged a combined 56.8 points per game this year. Losing both in the same series opener is about as brutal a hand as a playoff team can be dealt. Full Lakers vs. Rockets Injury Report Luka Dončić: Out — Grade 2 left hamstring strain (recently returned from treatment in Spain; no timetable for return this series) Austin Reaves: Out — Grade 2 left oblique strain (targeting early May; Round 1 return unlikely) Jaxson Hayes: Day-to-day — foot injury (expected to be available) LeBron James: Active — cleared after recent illness Kevin Durant: Questionable — right knee contusion (team remains optimistic) Fred VanVleet: Out for season — ACL repair Steven Adams: Out for season — left ankle surgery Without Dončić and Reaves, LeBron James becomes the unquestioned focal point of everything Los Angeles does offensively. Head coach JJ Redick is expected to expand the backcourt rotation, leaning on Luke Kennard and potentially Bronny James to share ball-handling responsibilities alongside LeBron. Deandre Ayton and Rui Hachimura will also need to provide consistent secondary scoring to keep opposing defenses honest. It’s a significant ask against a Houston squad that boasts one of the top defensive units in the league. Lakers vs Rockets Stats Los Angeles Lakers: LeBron James: 20.9 PPG, 6.1 REB, 7.2 AST, 0.6 BLK in 60 games Deandre Ayton: 12.5 PPG, 8.0 REB, 1.0 BLK in 72 games Rui Hachimura: 11.5 PPG, 3.3 REB in 68 games Houston Rockets: Kevin Durant: 26.0 PPG, 5.5 REB, 4.8 AST in 78 games (questionable) Alperen Sengun: 20.4 PPG, 8.9 REB, 6.2 AST in 72 games Amen Thompson: 18.3 PPG, 7.8 REB, 5.3 AST in 79 games Jabari Smith Jr.: 15.8 PPG, 6.9 REB in 77 games Reed Sheppard: 13.5 PPG, 3.4 AST in 82 games Can the Lakers Still Win the Series? The short answer is yes — but the path just got dramatically narrower. Los Angeles holds a 2-1 edge in the regular-season series and has dominated this playoff rivalry historically, winning six of nine all-time postseason matchups and each of the last four series between these franchises. Home court tonight at Crypto.com Arena gives them a meaningful edge. But a Lakers team without Dončić and Reaves is a fundamentally different beast than the one that went 16-2 in a dominant February-March stretch. Houston enters tonight as the favorite, and if Kevin Durant suits up despite his knee contusion, the Rockets will have a significant advantage at every position on the floor. Game 1 tips off tonight. LeBron has carried heavier loads before — the question is whether this roster around him is built to survive what’s coming.
